gloss: to bear fruit; to ripen; to come to fruition

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {実|みの}っていませんでした

definitions.explanation: For plants to produce mature fruit or grain.

definitions.gloss: to come to fruition; to produce results
definitions.explanation: For efforts or plans to yield positive outcomes.

examples.japanese: {実|みの}る⟦ほど→程：01724_hodo⟧⟦{頭|こうべ}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{垂|た}れる→垂れる：10075_tareru⟧⟦{稲穂|いなほ}→稲穂：10175_inaho⟧⟦かな→かな：10989_kana⟧。
examples.english: The more the rice ripens, the more it bows its head.
examples.notes: Well-known proverb teaching that accomplished people remain humble

examples.japanese: ⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{実|みの}る。
⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ついに→遂に：02360_tsuini⟧{実|みの}った。
examples.english: Years of hard work have finally borne fruit.

examples.japanese: ⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}けてきて→続ける：01231_tsuzukeru⟧、⟦やっと→やっと：01561_yatto⟧⟦{成果|せいか}→成果：06745_seika⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{実|みの}り⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: After continuing my research, results are finally starting to materialize.

notes:
{実|みの}る is intransitive (⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧). There is no common transitive pair.

ASPECT (ている):
{実|みの}っている indicates the resulting state of having borne fruit.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{稲|いね}→稲：01820_ine⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{実|みの}る (rice ripens)
- ⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{実|みの}る (efforts bear fruit)
- ⟦{愛|あい}→愛：02370_ai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{実|みの}る (love comes to fruition)
- 〜⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{実|みの}る: What bears fruit or produces results

PROVERB:
「{実|みの}る⟦ほど→程：01724_hodo⟧⟦{頭|こうべ}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{垂|た}れる→垂れる：10075_tareru⟧⟦{稲穂|いなほ}→稲穂：10175_inaho⟧⟦かな→かな：10989_kana⟧」 is a well-known saying teaching that truly accomplished people remain humble.

The figurative usage (⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{実|みの}る — efforts bear fruit) is very common and carries a positive connotation of success after hard work.
